question: The ‘Make in India’ programme, which started in 2014, is similar to _____________ of the 1970s and 1980s in India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Import Substitution policy**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ‘**Make in India’ programme** aims to **encourage companies to manufacture their products in India and boost domestic manufacturing capabilities.**
 
• This **aligns with the idea of import substitution policy, **which focuses on reducing dependency on imported goods by promoting the production of goods domestically.
 
• However, unlike the restrictive approach of the import substitution policies in the 1970s and 1980s,
 
• **‘Make in India’ promotes industrial growth **with an emphasis on ease of doing business, attracting foreign investments, and integrating into global supply chains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Make in India program aims to convert India to a self-reliant country and to give the Indian economy global recognition.
 
• The Make in India program was started on 25th September 2014.
 
• It was launched by the prime minister of India Narendra Modi.
 
• It was launched during the 12th five-year planning in India.
 
• The Make in India is organized by the government of India.
 
• The main objectives of the Make in India program are:
 
 
• Enforcement of secondary and tertiary sectors in India.
 
• Manufacturing of products in India and sell the products worldwide.
 
• Creating job opportunities for more than 10 million people.
 
• Boosting of India's GDP, trade, and economic growth.
